NAME: UART verification plan
details: Source: GARUDA-UART-SPEC-001, section 2 (requirements), section 10 (assertions) and section 11 (verification plan), written with the specification. Moved into vPlanner form on 2026-10-04; section 4 holds what the 2026-10-04 flow run added.

NAME: Requirements
details: From section 2 of the specification; planned tests from section 11.

NAME: R-1 Transmit and receive 8N1 frames at a programmable baud rate ...
details: Transmit and receive 8N1 frames at a programmable baud rate, byte-accurate in both directions.
implementation_note: Source: SYS §6.4

NAME: t_uart_tx_byte
details: Oracle: the model decodes what the DUT transmits
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-1] [N-7.2] the terminal received one frame, it was 0x41, stop bit high - 3 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_rx_byte
details: Oracle: the DUT receives what the model transmits
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-1] [N-7.3] LSR[0] set, RBR returned 0x5A, the read popped the FIFO - 3 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_loopback
details: Oracle: 256 bytes both ways, no loss or reorder
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: PARTLY IMPLEMENTED - tb/uart/tb_uart.sv runs 32 bytes each way, not the 256 the plan states: [R-1] 32 bytes in, 32 bytes out, all 32 correct and in order, no framing violation - 4 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_parity
details: Oracle: a clean 8E1 frame carries data and raises no error
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-7] a clean 8E1 frame sets no parity error, [R-1] and carries its data, [R-1] 8E1 transmit four frames - 3 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-2 115200 baud from pclk = 125 MHz with 1 baud error.
details: 115200 baud from pclk = 125 MHz with ≤1% baud error.
implementation_note: Source: TRM §3.5

NAME: t_uart_baud
details: Oracle: measured bit period at divisor 1084 is 8.68 µs ±1%
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks tagged [R-2] (bit period 8680 ns at divisor 1084, within 1 percent; also divisors 134, 2169, 13020) - 6 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-3 Word-only APB every register is 32 bits at a word-aligned offset ...
details: Word-only APB: every register is 32 bits at a word-aligned offset, even though upstream is byte-addressed.
implementation_note: Source: AHB2APB [N-7.12]

NAME: t_uart_wordmap
details: Oracle: each word offset reaches the intended 16550 register
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-3] [N-6.1] LCR at word offset 0x0C and [R-3] DLAB=0 offset 0x04 is IER - 2 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_dlab
details: Oracle: 0x00/0x04 bank correctly, and PRDATA[31:8] is 0
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-3] [N-6.2a] DLL and DLM under DLAB=1 and [R-3] [N-6.2] PRDATA[31:8] reads 0 - 3 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-4 Never stall the APB bus.
details: Never stall the APB bus.
implementation_note: Source: AHB2APB [N-7.15]

NAME: t_uart_pready
details: Oracle: PREADY high in every cycle of every access, FIFO full and empty
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, check [R-4] PREADY high in every cycle of every access (the run includes the TX-FIFO-full and RX-FIFO-full sequences) - 1 check, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-5 One held level interrupt per instance to its CLIC ID.
details: One held, level interrupt per instance to its CLIC ID.
implementation_note: Source: CLIC §7.2, D-17

NAME: t_uart_irq
details: Oracle: held ≥50 pclk, drops only on W1C
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks tagged [R-5] (asserted, still asserted 60 pclk later, W1C alone does not clear it, IRQEN masks) - 7 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-6 DMA request acknowledge on the instance s channel one beat per ...
details: DMA request/acknowledge on the instance's channel, one beat per assertion, word-sized beats carrying one byte in [7:0].
implementation_note: Source: DMA §7.3, D-21

NAME: t_uart_dma
details: Oracle: dma_req_checker; and no request while DLAB is set
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks tagged [R-6], [R-6a], [N-7.6] and [N-7.6b] (request withdrawn while DLAB is set), with dma_req_checker - 13 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-7 Report parity and framing errors to firmware without losing ...
details: Report parity and framing errors to firmware without losing received data.
implementation_note: Source: SYS §6.4

NAME: t_uart_parity_err
details: Oracle: a wrong-parity frame sets LSR[2] and IRQSTAT[2], and still delivers the byte
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-7] LSR[2] flags the parity error, [R-7] [N-7.5a] IRQSTAT[2] captured it, the byte is still delivered - 3 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_frame_err
details: Oracle: a low stop bit sets LSR[3] and the same event
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-7] LSR[3] flags a low stop bit, [R-7] [N-7.5a] the same line-error event, the byte is still delivered - 3 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_err_noleak
details: Oracle: neither flag leaks into the following byte
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks [R-7] the error does not leak into the following byte (parity and framing), and that byte is itself correct - 4 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-8 tx high (line idle) from reset until firmware acts rx ...
details: tx high (line idle) from reset until firmware acts; rx synchronised before use.
implementation_note: Source: Board safety, D-14

NAME: t_uart_reset
details: Oracle: tx high out of reset
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks tagged [R-8] (tx high in and out of reset) - 2 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: R-9 Three instances are independent no shared register interrupt DMA ...
details: Three instances are independent: no shared register, interrupt, DMA channel or clock enable.
implementation_note: Source: §1.1

NAME: t_chip_uart
details: Oracle: three instances, three windows, three CLIC IDs, no crosstalk
implementation_note: Status in the specification: new. Bench: sw/chip/t_chip_uart.c on tb/soc/tb_chip.sv (three UARTs through the pins; sim/chip_uart/run.log RESULT: PASSED); their three interrupt lines to their CLIC IDs in sw/chip/t_chip_integ.c (RESULT: PASSED); no-crosstalk checks tagged [R-9] in tb/uart/tb_uart.sv - 9 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: Planned tests not tied to one requirement
t_uart_baud_tol
details: Oracle: measures the mismatch the receiver tolerates: at least ±6% ([N-8.1])
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, check [N-8.1] receiver tolerance, measured -6.0 to +6.0 percent - 1 check, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_b2b
details: Oracle: 16 frames with no inter-frame gap — the timing patch 0001 changes ([N-8.2])
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, checks tagged [N-8.2] (16 back-to-back frames, none framed badly) - 2 checks, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: t_uart_rxidle
details: Oracle: rx synchroniser resets high, so no garbage byte at power-on ([N-9.3])
implementation_note: Status in the specification: pass. Bench: tb/uart/tb_uart.sv, check [N-9.2] [N-9.3] LSR is 0x60 out of reset, no garbage byte - 1 check, all PASS in the 2026-10-04 regression.

NAME: Assertions
details: From section 10 of the specification.

NAME: a_pready
details: PREADY is never low - the 16-pclk bridge timeout would fault the access
implementation_note: assert property in specification section 10. NOT IMPLEMENTED as SVA. Checked procedurally in tb/uart/tb_uart.sv ([R-4] PREADY high in every cycle of every access).

NAME: a_irq_held
details: the interrupt is a level: it may only fall on an IRQSTAT write
implementation_note: assert property in specification section 10. NOT IMPLEMENTED as SVA. Checked procedurally in tb/uart/tb_uart.sv ([R-5] still asserted 60 pclk later; [R-5] [N-7.5] W1C alone does not clear it).

NAME: a_dma_drop
details: one beat per request (D-16)
implementation_note: assert property in specification section 10. NOT IMPLEMENTED as SVA. Checked procedurally in tb/uart/tb_uart.sv ([R-6] dma_req drops after the ack; [N-7.6] the request drops for at least one pclk after every ack, 20 beats; dma_req_checker clean).

NAME: a_dma_dlab
details: the divisor latch is never a DMA target
implementation_note: assert property in specification section 10. NOT IMPLEMENTED as SVA. Checked procedurally in tb/uart/tb_uart.sv ([N-7.6b] the request is withdrawn while DLAB is set).

NAME: Added in the 2026-10-04 run
details: Checks added and defects found when the flow was run in order on 2026-10-04 (Docs/BUGS.md section 1h).

NAME: UART-3 baud counter stalls on a smaller divisor
details: The vendored baud counter compares for equality: a smaller divisor written while a frame is in flight leaves it counting to the 16-bit wrap, and the line stalls for up to 65 536 pclk.
implementation_note: OPEN (vendored IP, rtl/third_party/pulp/apb_uart_sv). Firmware rule: wait for LSR.TEMT before writing DLL or DLM. The bench now does so (wait_temt).

NAME: TB-28 line-status checks changed the divisor mid-frame
details: New line-status checks changed the divisor under a frame still being sent, which is how UART-3 was found.
implementation_note: FIXED (testbench): the checks wait for TEMT first; PASS.

NAME: Bench checks added
details: The bench grew from 53 to 116 checks (sim/tb_uart/run.log: checks=116 FAIL=0): word lengths 5 to 8, stop bits, FIFO full and overrun, four baud rates, break handling, TEMT timing, unimplemented registers.
